questions.q: Which of these is an enterprise platform this lesson names that combines a data catalog with automated lineage capture?
options: A plain text wiki page
The LTV Academy course outline
OpenLineage
Microsoft Purview
questions.explain: Microsoft Purview scans an organization's data estate and automatically builds a lineage map from what it finds, alongside Collibra and Alation as similar enterprise platforms.

questions.q: What does the dbt lineage graph shown in this lesson's real screenshot get generated from?
options: A manually drawn diagram uploaded by the user
Every ref() call between models, automatically
An entirely separate third-party lineage tool
A random sample of warehouse rows
questions.explain: The guide and script both describe the screenshot as dbt's own lineage graph, generated automatically from ref() calls between models, not hand-drawn.

questions.q: What is Apache Atlas, as described in this lesson?
options: A file format for storing lineage diagrams
An open-source metadata and governance framework originally built for the Hadoop ecosystem
A proprietary enterprise catalog sold exclusively by Microsoft
A business glossary term, not a tool
questions.explain: Apache Atlas is named as an open-source framework from the Hadoop ecosystem, used to track metadata and lineage for tools like Hive and Kafka.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe OpenLineage, and how is it different from a product like Collibra or Alation?
options: It is a deprecated standard with no current integrations
It is a specific feature inside Microsoft Purview only
It is a paid enterprise product that directly competes with Collibra
It's an open specification for structuring and sharing lineage metadata between tools, not a product you install
questions.explain: OpenLineage is described as a shared format/specification that different pipeline tools like Airflow and Spark can emit lineage events in, rather than a destination tool of its own.

questions.q: Why does this lesson deliberately avoid listing every feature of every named tool?
options: Because listing features is against this course's licensing agreement
Because only one tool in the entire industry supports lineage
Because tool capabilities change over time, and stating something inaccurate about a specific vendor is worse than staying general and verifiable
Because none of the named tools actually support lineage
questions.explain: The lesson sticks to well-established, verifiable capabilities by category rather than claiming specific features that could be outdated or inaccurate, and tells the learner to verify against current vendor docs before relying on any of it.
